title: Motus receipt v1
description: What a holder presents to a verifier: a RUN, as the ordered chain of segments it actually was, each segment carrying the commitments that bound it and the proof that each is inside a sealed window. It travels alone, so it declares its own version. ADR-021 decision 7: a receipt carrying only the checkpoint and the transaction proves a checkpoint and not a run. ADR-023 decision 1: a run made of segments is verified by walking them, so the format has to be able to hold more than one.

mode.description: What this receipt claims, for the run as a whole. LOCAL: the commitments are in a chain. WITNESSED: an independent party acknowledged the run's first BEGIN before it executed. QUALIFIED: witnessed plus identity and a qualified timestamp, neither of which this distribution produces.

segments.description: Oldest first. One entry per execution: the original, then each resume. Every segment has a BEGIN; only the LAST may have an END, because a segment that reached a terminal record cannot be resumed (UnsafeResume) and therefore cannot have a successor.

anchors.description: Zero or more. Each names the checkpoint it published, so a verifier can tell which segment it covers rather than assuming it covers the run.

attestations.description: Zero or more, and absent and empty mean the same thing: nobody asserted anything. An attestation is an ISSUER's signed assertion about a digest in this receipt (ADR-031) — verification material whose cryptography this validator never checks, reported as CLAIMED. It stays optional at 1.0.0: a receipt at levels 1-4 with no party involved is the common case.

Attestation.description: ADR-031 decision 3. An issuer's signed assertion: WHAT (the subject's digest) was asserted, WHO (issuer), WHEN (issued_at — the issuer's claim, not ours), and the material to verify it (proof, REQUIRED, shape fixed per type). Seven fields, no signature: for a timestamp token the signature IS the token inside proof.token_der.

subject.description: WHAT is asserted about: a checkpoint digest or the run root IN THIS RECEIPT (rule P9).

proof.description: Strict plain JSON (J1). The verification material, required, shape fixed per type below.

token_der.description: Base64 of the COMPLETE TimeStampResp (RFC 3161) — the certificate-bearing DER three commands verify: `openssl ts -reply -in response.tsr -token_out -out token.p7`, `openssl pkcs7 -inform DER -in token.p7 -print_certs -out certs.pem`, then `openssl ts -verify -in response.tsr -digest <message_imprint> -CAfile certs.pem`. Bounded (ADR-031 decision 3): the maxLength is the base64 of 2 MiB, which is already far past a real token's size.

message_imprint.description: The SHA-256 the TSA actually signed: sha256(bytes of `subject`'s digest value) — RFC 3161 hashes the datum being stamped, and here that datum is itself a digest, so the imprint is a hash of a hash. The validator recomputes it from `subject` and refuses a token that is not shown to be about it (P10).

proof.description: An rfc3161_timestamp attestation whose proof has no token is an attestation nobody can check: the signature IS the token, and no token means no signature (ADR-031 decision 3).

then.description: The proof shape is fixed per type the way $defs.Anchor fixes reference and published_at for anchored.

Execution.description: ADR-027 decision 4: the execution locator and canonical fingerprint. `ref` locates the original BEGIN; `fingerprint` is the Trace.root (null while the execution has no terminal record), never a receipt or partial-trace digest. `run_id` is carried for the embedder's correlation and is NOT a key. Optional until schema_version 1.0.0; required from 1.0.0.

Entry.description: One commitment, the path proving it is in a sealed window, and the checkpoint that sealed it. The three travel together because a proof without its checkpoint proves nothing and a checkpoint without a path proves somebody else's window.

proof.description: Siblings from leaf to root, each tagged with the side it sits on. An empty path is legal and means a single-leaf window.

Segment.description: One execution. `end` is absent for a segment that reached no terminal record — a crash, or a driver abandoned mid-iteration — which is ADR-020's residual class and the ordinary shape of every predecessor of a resumed run. Its absence is a fact, not a gap to be filled in.

Anchor.description: Where a checkpoint was published, and whether that has finished. `state: pending` is an intention and proves nothing; only `anchored` with a reference supports EXISTENCE.

then.description: An anchor that says `anchored` and names no transaction has published nothing anybody can look up.
